answer: Sybil resistance needs work tied to one verifiable identity, not to many cheap copies. Each agent stakes reputation earned through ferrous-stamped tasks: completed jobs are signed, timestamped, and linked so a clone army cannot replay the same proof twice. A relic check compares new submissions against the agent's own history and against peers, flagging identical outputs submitted under different names. Finally a reef of peer attestations confirms the work was real before any reward is released, so creating extra identities costs more than it earns.
